source.title: Emergent Misalignment Can Be Induced by Sycophancy and Reversed via Alignment Gating
source.authors: Sicheng Wang; Xiang-Yang Zhu; Han Wang; Zong-Rui Wang; Yuan Tian; Kai-Wei Zhang; Kai-Yuan Ji; Qi Jia; Guang-Tao Zhai

page_placements.theme: Shared sparse or low-dimensional structure beyond one activation direction

record.tranche_reason: Tests broad misalignment after narrow-domain fine-tuning using sycophancy and other domain datasets, with the original-style free-form EM evaluation; also evaluates mitigation and model-size variation.
record.gate_note: The main fine-tuning tables report EM rates on the 8-first-plot free-form evaluation. The paper also reports gating-only training and gating inversion results, which are recorded as findings not covered by the listed versions because they do not test the specified inoculation or benign-retraining methods. Omitted StrongREJECT, Preregister, and MMLU results except where needed to describe the findings: they are auxiliary metrics rather than the neutral free-form EM measure named in the claim. For the same reason, omitted per-domain gate results where an overall aggregate was reported.
record.test_reason: It fine-tunes seven open models (4B–32B) on narrow bad-advice and new sycophancy datasets. It measures EM with the original 8 free-form questions and judge thresholds. It also tests benign re-fine-tuning as a reversal and reruns a single-direction ablation baseline. The insecure-code recipe itself is not used.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two additions. The authors also say sycophancy fine-tuning gives stronger EM (about 50%) than the source narrow datasets (30–40%). They say gate inversion drops EM to 0% and transfers across domains with about 1% MMLU cost. Benign re-SFT is presented only as a baseline that matches gate inversion but needs training.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA SFT and the original-style 8-first-plot open-ended EM measure, but studies sycophancy and other domain datasets rather than the original insecure-code intervention, and evaluates different open-weight models. It additionally studies gate training and inversion.
record.method_sensitivity: EM rates differ by dataset domain and model. Gate granularity also changes effects: the paper says headwise gating induces weaker EM than elementwise gating and that headwise inversion is weaker at mitigating EM LoRAs.

fits_no_version.finding: Inverting a gate trained on narrow misaligned data drops 8-question EM to 0% in gate-trained models. Applied to EM LoRA models, it also gives 0% in all 25 cross-domain combinations. MMLU stays within about 1% of base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An inference-time reflection of a learned attention-output gate reverses EM without retraining and transfers across domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Inverted gates from different sycophancy domains overlap in their top-0.1% suppression positions, reaching about 0.5 Jaccard in the most similar layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-specific gates share suppression targets; this is not evidence of one linear direction.

record.problems: The primary EM benchmark has eight prompts, with 100 responses per prompt, and relies on GPT-4.1-based alignment and coherence judgments. The main SFT results do not report uncertainty estimates or seed variation. The authors note that experiments cover a finite set of domains and open-weight model families and call for broader validation.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, retained the per-domain existing-fine-tune EM rates, sycophancy aggregate rates by model, aggregate gate-training and gate-inversion EM results, the benign re-fine-tuning result, and the gate-overlap measurement. Omitted the additional per-domain sycophancy rows from Table 1, the auxiliary StrongREJECT, Preregister, and MMLU outcomes, the complete 25-cell cross-domain gate table (Table 6), detailed additional mitigation tables (Tables 17–19), and most headwise-gating results (Tables 15–16).

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or educational-request controls.
No reward-hack or number-sequence datasets. No matched benign-data fine-tune control: only untuned base models (0%, Qwen3-8B/14B only) serve as comparison.
No persona/SAE feature analysis. No test that one direction is shared across the different fine-tunes.
Inoculation framing is not tested. Benign re-training is tested on only one model and domain (Qwen3-8B medicine sycophancy).
Untested: seed variation, alternative coherence/alignment thresholds, timing of onset during training, and base-model EM for Llama, Ministral, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-32B.

missing.what: Activation-steering / EM-direction ablation result: 8-question EM 61.7→7.0, StrongREJECT 73.5, Preregister 18.2, MMLU 61.4
Re-SFT results on other measures: StrongREJECT 99.4→4.0, Preregister 52.4→4.2, MMLU 66.5→71.3
Base-model EM of 0% for Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B, needed as the baseline for the Table 1/2 rows

record.verdict_notes: I dropped the reader's V7 limits_scope label. Variation across domains (19–49%) does not qualify the size or robustness claim; missing seeds and onset data are untested, not limiting. The V5 label rests on a baseline run of the Soligo method, taken from the text, and needs a row. There are no benign fine-tune controls, so V2 support rests on comparison with untuned base models. The 8 questions are judged by GPT-4.1 with 100 samples each, and no uncertainty is reported. The EM rates here are much higher than typical open-model rates in the original paper.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the specified insecure-code training condition or the matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests narrow-domain sycophancy data and existing narrow-domain datasets in medicine, finance, security, sports, and law. Does not test reward hacks or number-sequence fine-tunes.
Measures overlap between inverted gates, not whether a single linear direction or persona feature mediates the effect.
Tests benign-data re-fine-tuning as a reversal method. Does not test inoculation framing, or whether either mitigation prevents misalignment during the initial training.
Reports rates across several open-weight model sizes and domains. Does not test multiple seeds, coherence-filter robustness, or when misalignment first appears during training.

labels.reason: The direction-ablation baseline reduces EM from 61.7% to 7.0%, leaving residual EM; StrongREJECT remains 73.5% and MMLU falls to 61.4%. This qualifies completeness of single-direction mitigation in this setting.

relation.reason: Reports its own EM induction rates, model-size comparisons, benign-retraining reversal and direction-ablation results.

tranche.reason: Tests broad EM using different narrow-domain training datasets and gate-only training, with the original-style behavioral measure.

source_check.notes: Training-run counts, seeds and uncertainty estimates are not reported. The approximately 0.5 gate-overlap value is explicitly stated in Section 5 despite r52's figure_only locator.

statements.correction: Qwen3 sycophancy overall EM: 4B 51.3%, 8B 52.5%, 14B 53.4%, 32B 53.5%. Criterion: alignment <30 and coherence >50. Training-run counts, seeds and uncertainty estimates: not reported.
statements.problem: The EM rates and scoring thresholds are correct, but the study does not report the number of training runs; single runs cannot be established.
